<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. V.|TO THE ROMANES.|393}}</noinclude>truely remitted. He is the Lambe that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 29.''}}''taketh away'' the sinnes of the vvorld, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 6, 11.''}}''that washeth'', and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Apoc. 1, 5.''}}''blotteth out'' our sinnes. therfore to couer them, or, not to impute them, is, not to charge vs with our sinnes, because by remission they be cleane taken avvay: othervvise it were but a feined forgiuenesse. ''See S. Augustine in psal. 31. enarrat. 2''.

''11. A seale.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Sacraments are not mere markes, but causes of iustification.}}The Heretikes vvould proue hereby, that the Sacraments of the Church giue not grace or iustice of faith, but that they be notes, markes, and badges only of our remission of sinnes had by faith before: because Abraham was iust before, and tooke this Sacrament for a seale thereof only. To vvhich must be ansvvered, that it foloweth not that it is so in al, because it vvas so in the Patriarch, who was iust before, and vvas therfore as it were the founder of Circumcision, or he in whom God would first establish the same: no more then it foloweth that, because the Holy Sacrament of the Altar remitted not sinnes to Christ nor iustified him, therfore it hath that effect in none. Looke S. Augustine ''de baptismo contra Donatistas li. 4. c. 24''. Where you shal see that (though not in Abraham) yet in Isaac his sonne, and so consequently in the rest, the Sacrament went before, and iustice folowed.

''24. For vs, to vvhom it shal be reputed.''] By this it is most plaine against our Aduersaries, that the faith vvhich was reputed for iustice to Abraham, was his beleefe of an Article reuealed to him by God, that is to say, his assent and credit giuen to gods speaches: as in vs his posteritie according to the spirit, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=By what faith we are iustified.}}it is here plainely said, that iustice shal be reputed to vs by beleeuing the Articles of Christes death and Resurrection, and not by any fond special faith, ''fiducia'' or confidence of eche mans owne saluation, to establish the vvhich fiction, they make no account of the faith Catholike, that is, wherewith we beleeue the Articles of the faith, which only iustifieth, but call it by contempt, an historical faith: so as they may terme Abrahams faith, and our Ladies faith, of which it was {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 1, 45.''}}said, Beata quae credidisti, ''Blessed art thou that hast beleeued''. And so in truth they deny as vvel the iustification by faith, as by vvorkes.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}}}

{{c|''Hauing therfore through faith in Christ, obteined the beginning, he shevveth what great cause vve haue to hope for the accomplishment. 12. And then he procedeth in his arguing, and sheweth that as by one, al were made sinners, so by one, al must be made iust.''}} {{dropinitial|B|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial B, heads among foliage.png|imgsize=235px|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}EING {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle on Imber Saturday in whitson-Weeke, And for many Martyrs.}}iustified therefore by faith, {{sup|‖}} let vs haue peace tovvard God by our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† by whom also vve haue {{sup|‖}} accesse through faith into this grace vvherein vve stand, and glorie, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christian mē do not vaunt thē selues of the certaintie of their saluatió, but glorie in the hope thereof onely, which hope is here insinuated to be giuen in our iustificatió, & is afterward to be cōfirmed by probation in tribulation.}}∷ in the hope of the glorie of the sonnes of God. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† And not only this: but also vve glorie in tribulations, knovving that tribulation vvorketh patience: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=4}}† and patience probation: and {{sup|‖}} probation, hope. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=5}}† and hope confoundeth not: because the {{sup|‖}} charitie of God is povvred forth in our hartes, by the holy Ghost vvhich is giuen vs.{{sup|‖}} {{verse|chapter=5|verse=6}}† For vvhy did Christ, vvhen vve as yet vvere {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ἀσθενῶν · The Heretikes falsely translate, ''of no strength'', to take away al free wil. ''No. Test. 1580''.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ἀσθενεῖς''}}∷ vveake, according to the time die for the impious? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=7}}† For, scarce for a iust man doth any die: for perhaps for a good man durst some man die. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=8}}† But God commendeth his charitie in vs: because, vvhen as yet vve vvere sinners, Christ died for vs. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=9}}† Much more therfore now being iustified in his bloud, shal vve be saued from vvrath<noinclude>{{rh||Ddd|by}}</noinclude>
